title: Number of Islands
keyIdea: Scan the grid; every unvisited '1' starts a new island. Flood it (BFS or DFS, 4 directions) marking every connected land cell visited, so it is counted once. Count the floods.

approaches.name: DFS that sinks the island
approaches.idea: On a '1': count++, then recursively turn it and all connected land into '0'.
approaches.why: Each cell is sunk at most once; no vis array, but it changes the grid.

approaches.name: BFS with a visited array
approaches.idea: On an unvisited '1': BFS with a queue, marking cells visited when pushed; count++ after each BFS.
approaches.why: Each cell is pushed and popped at most once.

quiz.q: Why does each BFS/DFS start mean exactly one new island?
options: The flood marks every cell of that island, so later scans skip all of them

quiz.q: Why mark a cell visited when pushing, not when popping?
options: So two neighbours can't both push the same cell
Popping is too late for counting
No, only up, down, left and right

quiz.q: How does the DFS version avoid a vis array?
options: It turns visited land into water ('0')
